parameters.content:
## ppwr-scope

Puts suppliers and their items into a campaign. Nothing else in this project does.

01 launches a campaign by reading `campaign_item` rows that are already sitting in `pending`. It never decides what belongs in a campaign. This is where that decision is made, and until it existed the only way to load one was to write a script.

**Upload a CSV, get a preview, then commit.** The whole file is checked before a single row is written, and what cannot be used comes back by line number with the reason. A load that quietly skips eleven rows is worse than one that refuses.

**Columns.** Required: `vendor_legal_name`, `vendor_contact_email`, `internal_sku`. Optional: `vendor_contact_name`, `vendor_country`, `vendor_language`, `description`, `packaging_level`, `primary_material`, `food_contact`, `intended_use`. Header order does not matter and unknown columns are ignored.

**Loading the same file twice is safe.** A supplier is matched on their contact email and an item on that supplier plus the SKU, which are the same keys the store enforces. The second run creates nothing and matches everything, so fixing three bad rows and uploading again is the normal way to work.

**The ruleset version has no default.** A campaign freezes it at launch and every submission runs against that version for as long as the campaign lives, so choosing one for you would be choosing which rules your suppliers answer.

**What it does not do.** It does not send anything. Items land in `pending` and stay there until you launch the campaign with 01.

Code nodes are built from `src/intake/` by `npm run bundle`.

### Read

A form upload or a scripted POST. Both end up at Scope request, which is the one name everything downstream reads the load from.

### Check

The whole file, against what already exists. No writes on this lane.

### Create

Suppliers, then their items, then the campaign row that puts each one in scope. In that order, because each stage needs the ids the one before it minted.

parameters.formDescription:
Upload a supplier list and this will tell you what it would create before it creates anything.

Required columns: vendor_legal_name, vendor_contact_email, internal_sku.
Optional: vendor_contact_name, vendor_country, vendor_language, description, packaging_level, primary_material, food_contact, intended_use.
